thread:
alice.k: Heads up — we need a rolling maintenance for the satellite GPU pools (eu-west-3 + apac-edge). Target window Tue 00:30-03:00 UTC. Goal: firmware + NIC driver bumps and a graceful node recycle with zero customer-requested downtime if possible.

brian.t: Are we doing cohort interleaving or full-pool waves?

alice.k: Interleaved cohorts: will cycle 10% of nodes per batch, wait 6m for health checks, then continue. Plan to keep 2 spare racks per region for burst backfill.

carmen_ops: Requesting we avoid triggering preemptible reclaim in the middle of the window. Can we pre-warm capacity?

li: Yes — we can provision ephemeral warm nodes in the us-east standby pool and route bursts via smart-router for up to 45m during the busiest batches. That costs ~0.6k USD/hr for the window.

mike_oncall: Any customer-facing impact expected? I flagged support so they can watch for slow starts.

alice.k: Minimal. We expect transient queueing for cold prefixes for ~10–30s on affected nodes until KV cache reseed finishes. No request 500s expected; fallbacks in place to spin to dedicated variants if latency spikes >250ms.

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance created: INC-2026-4123, channel #eng-infra, ETA Tue 00:30 UTC — see https://infra.internal/incidents/INC-2026-4123

brian.t: Runbook checklist please — cordon -> drain -> reboot -> nic-flash -> uncordon? Also health checks?

alice.k: Runbook (short):
```
1) cordon cohort
2) graceful drain tasks with --max-inflight=20
3) bootstrap driver+fw (2x attempts if flaky)
4) run `curl -sS http://localhost:4242/health | jq .` verify all subsystems
5) uncordon once metrics stable for 6m
```

carmen_ops: Add a step to warm KV cache: `kvseed --pool=satellite --prefix-weight=0.8` after boot. Also gate RNAT testing for egress.

li: Network constraints: apac-edge egress has a maintenance blackhole between 00:45-01:15 UTC for an upstream provider — we'll avoid heavy cross-region syncs during that window. Coordinate with backfills.

mike_oncall: If egress blackhole hits, fallback policy to route tenant traffic via eu-west-3 for API reads only, writes stay local. Is cross-region routing tested?

brian.t: We exercised cross-region read fallback in last year's drill. We should still run a quick canary during the first batch (2 nodes) and run synthetic prompt load for 15m.

alice.k: Agreed — canary plan: two satellite nodes -> run soak 15m with traffic-replay -> verify tail latency p95 < 300ms and error rate < 0.01%. If fail, abort and roll back cohort.

carmen_ops: Cost note: prewarming + standby routing adds ~0.8k USD for the night. If we need a rollback (full cohort re-add), add another ~1.2k. Putting that in the ops budget ticket.

li: Owner assignments: Alice (lead), Brian (network lead), Carmen (backfill/kv), Mike (on-call exec). I’ll update the maintenance doc and tag support.

mike_oncall: I'll be on-call for the window. Parking a pager rotation from 00:00-04:00 UTC.

alice.k: Final comms: Posting notify to #customer-impact 24h prior and #status pages 2h prior. Ops-bot will create a postmortem draft. Any objections?

brian.t: thumbs up from me.

carmen_ops: No objections. I’ll prep the KV prompt set for regression checks.

ops-bot: reminder: maintenance checklist due in 12h. 

alice.k: Thanks all — we’ll kick off a preflight checklist 2h before the window. If anyone sees capacity holes in the next 8h, ping me directly. :rocket:
